text: The probe weighed 1,850 kilograms at launch. Power came from two solar wings that together produced 900 watts near Veth. A xenon ion engine handled course corrections during the long cruise.

text: Aurelia's radar showed that the moon Osk has a liquid ocean beneath about 14 kilometers of ice. The probe also detected faint plumes of water vapor rising from cracks near the south pole of the moon Teb. These plumes were the first evidence that Teb is geologically active.

text: Contact with Aurelia was lost in November 2018 after a radiation storm damaged its main computer. The team had already received nearly all planned data. The probe was left in orbit around Veth and is expected to remain there for several centuries.

Brindle is a semi-hard cheese made in the Halden valley. It has a pale orange rind and a slightly sweet, nutty taste. Most wheels weigh about 9 kilograms.

section: Brindle Cheese > How it is made
text: Brindle is made from raw cow's milk collected within 15 kilometers of the dairy. The curds are cut to the size of rice grains and heated to 41 degrees Celsius. After pressing, the wheels are soaked in brine for two days.
embed_text:
brindle_cheese | Brindle Cheese > How it is made
Brindle is made from raw cow's milk collected within 15 kilometers of the dairy. The curds are cut to the size of rice grains and heated to 41 degrees Celsius. After pressing, the wheels are soaked in brine for two days.

text: Wheels are aged in limestone caves for a minimum of eight months. During aging, each wheel is turned by hand every week and brushed with a mixture of salt water and annatto. Wheels aged for more than eighteen months are sold as Brindle Reserve and cost roughly double the standard price.
embed_text:

Wheels are aged in limestone caves for a minimum of eight months. During aging, each wheel is turned by hand every week and brushed with a mixture of salt water and annatto. Wheels aged for more than eighteen months are sold as Brindle Reserve and cost roughly double the standard price.

text: Since 2004 the name Brindle has been protected, meaning only cheese made in the Halden valley may use it. The rule was introduced after imitation cheeses began appearing in foreign markets. Producers must pass an annual inspection to keep the right to use the name.

text: The Marlow Bridge crosses the Tessen River in the town of Orrin Vale. It was completed in 1923 and is 412 meters long. It is a steel arch bridge and carries a single railway line along with a pedestrian walkway.
embed_text:
marlow_bridge | The Marlow Bridge > Overview
The Marlow Bridge crosses the Tessen River in the town of Orrin Vale. It was completed in 1923 and is 412 meters long. It is a steel arch bridge and carries a single railway line along with a pedestrian walkway.

text: Construction began in 1917 under the engineer Halvard Pike. Work stopped for two years during the Great Flood of 1919, which swept away the first set of temporary supports. After the flood, Pike redesigned the foundations so that each pier rested on bedrock instead of river gravel. The redesign added eleven months to the schedule and raised the total cost to 3.2 million crowns.
embed_text:
marlow_bridge | The Marlow Bridge > History
Construction began in 1917 under the engineer Halvard Pike. Work stopped for two years during the Great Flood of 1919, which swept away the first set of temporary supports. After the flood, Pike redesigned the foundations so that each pier rested on bedrock instead of river gravel. The redesign added eleven months to the schedule and raised the total cost to 3.2 million crowns.

text: In 1987 the bridge was closed for repairs after inspectors found corrosion in the lower arch. The restoration took four years and replaced about a third of the original steel. The bridge reopened in 1991 with a new coat of green paint. Green was chosen because it matched the color of the surrounding pine forest.

text: Quill is a small scripting language designed for teaching. It was created by Ines Marchetti and first released in 2011. The language uses indentation to mark blocks and has only fourteen keywords.
embed_text:
quill_language | The Quill Programming Language > Overview
Quill is a small scripting language designed for teaching. It was created by Ines Marchetti and first released in 2011. The language uses indentation to mark blocks and has only fourteen keywords.

section: The Quill Programming Language > Design goals
text: Marchetti wanted beginners to read code almost like plain English. For that reason, Quill uses the word "say" to print output and "ask" to read input. Variables are declared with the keyword "hold". Error messages are written as full sentences that suggest a fix.
embed_text:
quill_language | The Quill Programming Language > Design goals
Marchetti wanted beginners to read code almost like plain English. For that reason, Quill uses the word "say" to print output and "ask" to read input. Variables are declared with the keyword "hold". Error messages are written as full sentences that suggest a fix.

section: The Quill Programming Language > Types and memory
text: Quill has four built-in types: number, text, list and flag. All values are checked when the program runs, not before. Memory is managed by reference counting, so a value is freed as soon as nothing uses it.
embed_text:

text: The standard interpreter is called quillrun. A web playground lets students run code without installing anything. Version 3.0, released in 2019, added a debugger that lets learners step through a program one line at a time.

text: Skerryball is a team sport played on small rocky islands off the northern coast. It was first played in 1923, the same year the Marlow Bridge opened, although the two have no connection. Each team has seven players and a match lasts three periods of twenty minutes.
embed_text:
skerryball | Skerryball > Overview
Skerryball is a team sport played on small rocky islands off the northern coast. It was first played in 1923, the same year the Marlow Bridge opened, although the two have no connection. Each team has seven players and a match lasts three periods of twenty minutes.

text: Players score by throwing a leather ball into a net fixed to a wooden post. The ball may not be carried for more than three steps. A player who touches the ball with a foot is penalized with a two-minute suspension. The post stands 2.4 meters high.

text: The national championship is called the Gull Cup. It is held every August on the island of Brae. The team from Fenwick has won the cup nine times, more than any other club. The most recent winner was the team from Dunmore in 2024.
